Class EventResolutionOverlay

java.lang.Object
view.widgets.EventResolutionOverlay
public final class EventResolutionOverlay extends Object
Themed modal overlay that presents event-resolution results one at a time.

Multiple events can be enqueued via enqueue(StackPane, EventResolutionDto); each is shown for 12.0 seconds with a visible countdown bar, then the next is displayed automatically. Clicking anywhere on the backdrop advances to the next event immediately.

The class is entirely static — it manages a single application-wide overlay state and cannot be instantiated.

      FIFO queue of events waiting to be shown. Events are added by enqueue(StackPane, EventResolutionDto) and consumed by showNext().

    • activeRoot

      private static javafx.scene.layout.StackPane activeRoot
      The StackPane scene root that currently hosts the active backdrop, or null when no overlay is visible.

    • activeBackdrop

      private static javafx.scene.layout.StackPane activeBackdrop
      The backdrop StackPane currently overlaying the scene, or null when no overlay is visible. Removed from activeRoot after the fade-out completes.

    • activeDwell

      private static javafx.animation.PauseTransition activeDwell
      The PauseTransition that fires advance() after DWELL_SECONDS seconds. Stopped and nulled whenever the overlay is dismissed early (by a click or reset()).

    • activeProgress

      private static javafx.animation.Timeline activeProgress
      The Timeline that animates the ProgressBar from full to empty over DWELL_SECONDS seconds. Started by startDwell() after the fade-in completes, so the bar and the dwell timer stay in sync.

    • onQueueDrained

      private static Runnable onQueueDrained
      One-shot callback invoked on the JavaFX Application Thread when the last overlay closes and queue becomes empty. Cleared after firing to prevent double invocation.

  • Method Details

    • isQueueEmpty

      public static boolean isQueueEmpty()
      Returns true when there are no events currently visible and no events waiting in the queue.
      Returns:
      true if the overlay system is fully idle

    • setOnQueueDrained

      public static void setOnQueueDrained(Runnable callback)
      Registers a one-shot callback that fires on the JavaFX Application Thread when the last overlay closes and the queue drains to empty.

      If the queue is already empty at the time of registration, the callback is invoked immediately rather than being stored.

      Parameters:
      callback - the Runnable to invoke when all overlays have been dismissed

    • enqueue

      public static void enqueue(javafx.scene.layout.StackPane root, EventResolutionDto dto)
      Adds an event to the display queue and starts showing it immediately if no other overlay is currently active. Silently ignores null arguments.
      Parameters:
      root - the StackPane scene root that will host the backdrop
      dto - the resolved-event data to display

    • reset

      public static void reset()
      Immediately stops all animations, removes the active backdrop from the scene, clears the pending queue, and resets all static state to its initial values.

      Any registered onQueueDrained callback is discarded without firing.

    • advance

      private static void advance()
      Cancels the current dwell timer and progress animation, then fades out the active backdrop before calling showNext(). If no backdrop is visible, calls showNext() directly.

      Invoked either by the dwell timer expiring or by a mouse click on the backdrop.

    • showNext

      private static void showNext()
      Polls the next EventResolutionOverlay.PendingEvent from queue and displays it. If the queue is empty, clears activeRoot and fires onQueueDrained (if registered). Otherwise:
      1. Closes any open TribePopupController popup.
      2. Builds the visual panel via buildPanel(EventResolutionDto).
      3. Creates a full-screen backdrop, wires a click handler to advance(), adds it to the scene root, and plays the fade-in animation.
      4. On fade-in completion, calls startDwell() to begin the timer.

    • startDwell

      private static void startDwell()
      Starts the countdown after the fade-in animation completes. Resumes activeProgress (the bar animation) and creates a PauseTransition for DWELL_SECONDS seconds that calls advance() when it expires.

    • buildPanel

      private static javafx.scene.layout.StackPane buildPanel(EventResolutionDto dto)
      Builds the full visual panel (stone-slab background + content overlay) for a single event. Also creates and assigns activeProgress, the Timeline that animates the countdown ProgressBar. The panel layout from top to bottom:
      1. Header row — event-type icon, title, and era label (buildHeader(EventResolutionDto)).
      2. Horizontal separator.
      3. One buildPlayerRow(PlayerEventDeltaDto) per entry in dto.deltas.
      4. 6 px gap.
      5. Countdown ProgressBar (4 px tall, drains left-to-right).
      6. Footer with "tap to continue" hint.
      Parameters:
      dto - the event data used to populate the panel
      Returns:
      the fully constructed slab StackPane ready to be added to a backdrop

    • buildStatBox

      private static javafx.scene.layout.HBox buildStatBox(String iconPath, int before, int after)
      Builds a small icon + value + delta HBox for a single stat (food or prestige). The delta label is styled green for positive changes, red for negative, and neutral for no change.
      Parameters:

      after - the stat value after the event was applied
